sanskrit: iti pṛṣṭo dvijais taiḥ sa prahasya nakulo 'bravīt naiṣānṛtā mayā vāṇī proktā darpeṇa vā dvijāḥ
english: Thus questioned by those twice-born, the mongoose laughed and said: "No false word have I spoken, O brāhmaṇas, nor anything said out of arrogance."

sanskrit: yan mayoktam idaṃ kiṃ cid yuṣmābhiś cāpy upaśrutam saktuprasthena vo nāyaṃ yajñas tulyo narādhipāḥ uñchavṛtter vadānyasya kurukṣetranivāsinaḥ
english: "What little I have said, and what you too have heard from me — that this sacrifice of yours, O kings, is not equal to a measure of barley-meal given by a generous gleaner who dwelt in Kurukṣetra —

sanskrit: ity avaśyaṃ mayaitad vo vaktavyaṃ dvijapuṃgavāḥ śṛṇutāvyagramanasaḥ śaṃsato me dvijarṣabhāḥ
english: "this I must surely tell you, O bulls among the twice-born. Listen with undistracted minds as I relate it, O foremost of brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: anubhūtaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ ca yan mayādbhutam uttamam uñchavṛtter yathāvṛttaṃ kurukṣetranivāsinaḥ
english: "It is the supreme marvel that I myself experienced and witnessed — what befell that gleaner who dwelt in Kurukṣetra,

sanskrit: svargaṃ yena dvijaḥ prāptaḥ sabhāryaḥ sasutasnuṣaḥ yathā cārdhaṃ śarīrasya mamedaṃ kāñcanīkṛtam
english: "by which deed a brāhmaṇa attained heaven together with his wife, his son and his daughter-in-law, and by which this half of my body here was turned to gold."

sanskrit: nakula uvāca hanta vo vartayiṣyāmi dānasya paramaṃ phalam nyāyalabdhasya sūkṣmasya vipradattasya yad dvijāḥ
english: The mongoose said: "Come then, I shall recount to you the supreme fruit of a gift — a slender gift, righteously obtained and bestowed upon a brāhmaṇa, O twice-born ones."

sanskrit: dharmakṣetre kurukṣetre dharmajñair bahubhir vṛte uñchavṛttir dvijaḥ kaś cit kāpotir abhavat purā
english: "In Kurukṣetra, the field of righteousness, peopled by many who knew the law, there once lived a certain brāhmaṇa who subsisted by gleaning, living after the manner of the pigeon."

sanskrit: sabhāryaḥ saha putreṇa sasnuṣas tapasi sthitaḥ vadhūcaturtho vṛddhaḥ sa dharmātmā niyatendriyaḥ
english: "With his wife, his son, and his daughter-in-law, he abode in austerity — a household of four, his daughter-in-law the fourth; aged, righteous of soul, his senses subdued."

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhe kāle tadā vipro bhuṅkte taiḥ saha suvrataḥ ṣaṣṭhe kāle kadā cic ca tasyāhāro na vidyate bhuṅkte 'nyasmin kadā cit sa ṣaṣṭhe kāle dvijottamaḥ
english: "That brāhmaṇa of firm vows would eat with them only at the sixth mealtime; and sometimes even at the sixth mealtime no food was to be had, so that the best of the twice-born would eat only at the next sixth mealtime."

sanskrit: kapotadharmiṇas tasya durbhikṣe sati dāruṇe nāvidyata tadā viprāḥ saṃcayas tān nibodhata kṣīṇauṣadhisamāvāyo dravyahīno 'bhavat tadā
english: "When a dreadful famine came upon him who lived by the pigeon's law, there was then no store laid by, O brāhmaṇas — mark this well. The stock of herbs was spent, and he was left without any provision."

sanskrit: kāle kāle 'sya saṃprāpte naiva vidyeta bhojanam kṣudhāparigatāḥ sarve prātiṣṭhanta tadā tu te
english: "As each mealtime came round, no food was to be found; and all of them, gripped by hunger, set out to glean."

sanskrit: uñchaṃs tadā śuklapakṣe madhyaṃ tapati bhāskare uṣṇārtaś ca kṣudhārtaś ca sa vipras tapasi sthitaḥ uñcham aprāptavān eva sārdhaṃ parijanena ha
english: "Gleaning in the bright fortnight while the sun blazed at midday, that brāhmaṇa, steadfast in austerity, tormented by heat and by hunger, gained no gleanings at all, he together with his household."

sanskrit: sa tathaiva kṣudhāviṣṭaḥ spṛṣṭvā toyaṃ yathāvidhi kṣapayām āsa taṃ kālaṃ kṛcchraprāṇo dvijottamaḥ
english: "Even thus possessed by hunger, the best of the twice-born, his life hanging by a thread, touched water according to the rite and so let that mealtime pass."

sanskrit: atha ṣaṣṭhe gate kāle yavaprastham upārjayat yavaprasthaṃ ca te saktūn akurvanta tapasvinaḥ
english: "Then, when the sixth mealtime had come, he earned a prastha-measure of barley; and from that prastha of barley those ascetics made meal."

sanskrit: kṛtajapyāhvikās te tu hutvā vahniṃ yathāvidhi kuḍavaṃ kuḍavaṃ sarve vyabhajanta tapasvinaḥ
english: "Having performed their daily prayers and offered to the fire according to the rite, those ascetics divided it all, a kuḍava-measure for each."

sanskrit: athāgacchad dvijaḥ kaś cid atithir bhuñjatāṃ tadā te taṃ dṛṣṭvātithiṃ tatra prahṛṣṭamanaso 'bhavan
english: "Then, as they were about to eat, a certain brāhmaṇa came as a guest; and seeing the guest there, they grew glad of heart."

sanskrit: te 'bhivādya sukhapraśnaṃ pṛṣṭvā tam atithiṃ tadā viśuddhamanaso dāntāḥ śraddhādamasamanvitāḥ
english: "They greeted him and asked after his welfare — pure of mind, self-controlled, endowed with faith and restraint,

sanskrit: anasūyavo gatakrodhāḥ sādhavo gatamatsarāḥ tyaktamānā jitakrodhā dharmajñā dvijasattamāḥ
english: "free of envy, free of anger, good men free of malice, having renounced pride, having conquered wrath — those excellent brāhmaṇas who knew the law."

sanskrit: sabrahmacaryaṃ svaṃ gotraṃ samākhyāya parasparam kuṭīṃ praveśayām āsuḥ kṣudhārtam atithiṃ tadā
english: "Having declared to one another their lineage and their course of sacred study, they ushered the hunger-stricken guest into their hut."

sanskrit: idam arghyaṃ ca pādyaṃ ca bṛsī ceyaṃ tavānagha śucayaḥ saktavaś ceme niyamopārjitāḥ prabho pratigṛhṇīṣva bhadraṃ te mayā dattā dvijottama
english: "'Here is water for your hands and water for your feet, and here is a seat of grass for you, O sinless one; and here is pure barley-meal, won by our observances, O lord. Accept it — blessings upon you — it is given by me, O best of the twice-born.'"

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratigṛhyātha saktūnāṃ kuḍavaṃ dvijaḥ bhakṣayām āsa rājendra na ca tuṣṭiṃ jagāma saḥ
english: "Thus addressed, the brāhmaṇa accepted that kuḍava of meal and ate it, O lord of kings; yet he did not attain satisfaction."

sanskrit: sa uñchavṛttiḥ taṃ prekṣya kṣudhāparigataṃ dvijam āhāraṃ cintayām āsa kathaṃ tuṣṭo bhaved iti
english: "The gleaner, observing that the brāhmaṇa was still gripped by hunger, fell to pondering about food: 'How might he be made content?'"

sanskrit: tasya bhāryābravīd rājan madbhāgo dīyatām iti gacchatv eṣa yathākāmaṃ saṃtuṣṭo dvijasattamaḥ
english: "His wife said to him, O king: 'Let my portion be given. Let this best of the twice-born depart contented, as he wishes.'"

sanskrit: iti bruvantīṃ tāṃ sādhvīṃ dharmātmā sa dvijarṣabhaḥ kṣudhāparigatāṃ jñātvā saktūṃs tān nābhyanandata
english: "But that righteous bull among brāhmaṇas, knowing that the virtuous woman who spoke thus was herself gripped by hunger, would not approve the giving of that meal."

sanskrit: jānan vṛddhāṃ kṣudhārtāṃ ca śrāntāṃ glānāṃ tapasvinīm tvagasthibhūtāṃ vepantīṃ tato bhāryām uvāca tām
english: "Knowing his wife to be aged, hunger-stricken, weary, faint, an ascetic woman reduced to skin and bone and trembling, he then said to her:"

sanskrit: api kīṭapataṃgānāṃ mṛgāṇāṃ caiva śobhane striyo rakṣyāś ca poṣyāś ca naivaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: "'Even among insects and winged creatures and beasts, O lovely one, the females are to be protected and nourished. You ought not to speak in this wise.'"

sanskrit: anukampito naro nāryā puṣṭo rakṣita eva ca prapated yaśaso dīptān na ca lokān avāpnuyāt
english: "'A man who is shown compassion by a woman, nourished and protected by her, would fall from his blazing renown and would not attain the higher worlds.'"

sanskrit: ity uktā sā tataḥ prāha dharmārthau nau samau dvija saktuprasthacaturbhāgaṃ gṛhāṇemaṃ prasīda me
english: "Thus addressed, she then said: 'Our merit and our purpose are alike, O brāhmaṇa. Take this quarter-part of the prastha of meal; be gracious to me.'"

sanskrit: satyaṃ ratiś ca dharmaś ca svargaś ca guṇanirjitaḥ strīṇāṃ patisamādhīnaṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ ca dvijottama
english: "'Truth, delight, righteousness, and heaven won by virtue — all that women desire depends upon the husband, O best of the twice-born.'"

sanskrit: ṛtur mātuḥ pitur bījaṃ daivataṃ paramaṃ patiḥ bhartuḥ prasādāt strīṇāṃ vai ratiḥ putraphalaṃ tathā
english: "'The season belongs to the mother, the seed to the father; the husband is the supreme deity. By the husband's grace come to women both delight and the fruit that is offspring.'"

sanskrit: pālanād dhi patis tvaṃ me bhartāsi bharaṇān mama putrapradānād varadas tasmāt saktūn gṛhāṇa me
english: "'Since you protect me, you are my husband; since you maintain me, you are my support; and since you have given me a son, you are my bestower of boons. Therefore take my meal.'"

sanskrit: jarāparigato vṛddhaḥ kṣudhārto durbalo bhṛśam upavāsapariśrānto yadā tvam api karśitaḥ
english: "'You too are overtaken by age and old, hunger-stricken and grievously weak, worn out by fasting and wasted away.'"

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tayā saktūn pragṛhyedaṃ vaco 'bravīt dvija saktūn imān bhūyaḥ pratigṛhṇīṣva sattama
english: "Thus addressed by her, he took the meal and spoke these words: 'O brāhmaṇa, accept this meal as well, O excellent one.'"

sanskrit: sa tān pragṛhya bhuktvā ca na tuṣṭim agamad dvijaḥ tam uñchavṛttir ālakṣya tataś cintāparo 'bhavat
english: "The brāhmaṇa took it and ate it, yet attained no satisfaction; and the gleaner, marking this, fell once more into anxious thought."

sanskrit: putra uvāca saktūn imān pragṛhya tvaṃ dehi viprāya sattama ity evaṃ sukṛtaṃ manye tasmād etat karomy aham
english: "The son said: 'Take this meal of mine and give it to the brāhmaṇa, O excellent father. This I deem a meritorious deed, and therefore I do it.'"

sanskrit: bhavān hi paripālyo me sarvayatnair dvijottama sādhūnāṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ hy etat pitur vṛddhasya poṣaṇam
english: "'For you are to be cherished by me with every effort, O best of the twice-born; this is the desire of good men — the sustaining of an aged father.'"

sanskrit: putrārtho vihito hy eṣa sthāvirye paripālanam śrutir eṣā hi viprarṣe triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā
english: "'For this is the very purpose of a son — protection in old age. This is the teaching, O sage among brāhmaṇas, renowned throughout the three worlds.'"

sanskrit: prāṇadhāraṇamātreṇa śakyaṃ kartuṃ tapas tvayā prāṇo hi paramo dharmaḥ sthito deheṣu dehinām
english: "'By merely keeping your life-breath, you can perform austerities; for the life-breath is the supreme duty, abiding in the bodies of embodied beings.'"

sanskrit: pitovāca api varṣasahasrī tvaṃ bāla eva mato mama utpādya putraṃ hi pitā kṛtakṛtyo bhavaty uta
english: "The father said: 'Even were you a thousand years old, you would still be reckoned a child by me; for a father, having begotten a son, becomes one who has fulfilled his task.'"

sanskrit: bālānāṃ kṣud balavatī jānāmy etad ahaṃ vibho vṛddho 'haṃ dhārayiṣyāmi tvaṃ balī bhava putraka
english: "'The hunger of the young is strong — this I know, my dear one. I am old, and I shall endure it. Keep your strength, my son.'"

sanskrit: jīrṇena vayasā putra na mā kṣud bādhate 'pi ca dīrghakālaṃ tapas taptaṃ na me maraṇato bhayam
english: "'With my years grown decayed, my son, hunger does not even afflict me; long have I practised austerity, and I have no fear of death.'"

sanskrit: putra uvāca apatyam asmi te putras trāṇāt putro hi viśrutaḥ ātmā putraḥ smṛtas tasmāt trāhy ātmānam ihātmanā
english: "The son said: 'I am your offspring, your son; and a son is so named because he saves. The son is held to be one's very self; therefore by your self save your self here.'"

sanskrit: pitovāca rūpeṇa sadṛśas tvaṃ me śīlena ca damena ca parīkṣitaś ca bahudhā saktūn ādadmi te tataḥ
english: "The father said: 'In form you are like me, and in character and in self-restraint; and I have tested you many times. Therefore I will take your meal.'"

sanskrit: ity uktvādāya tān saktūn prītātmā dvijasattamaḥ prahasann iva viprāya sa tasmai pradadau tadā
english: "So saying, that best of the twice-born, glad of soul, took the meal and, almost smiling, gave it then to the brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: bhuktvā tān api saktūn sa naiva tuṣṭo babhūva ha uñchavṛttis tu savrīḍo babhūva dvijasattamaḥ
english: "Yet even after eating that meal he was not satisfied; and the gleaner, that excellent brāhmaṇa, was overcome with shame."

sanskrit: taṃ vai vadhūḥ sthitā sādhvī brāhmaṇapriyakāmyayā saktūn ādāya saṃhṛṣṭā guruṃ taṃ vākyam abravīt
english: "Then the virtuous daughter-in-law, standing by, desiring to please the brāhmaṇa, gladly took up her meal and spoke this word to her elder:"

sanskrit: saṃtānāt tava saṃtānaṃ mama vipra bhaviṣyati saktūn imān atithaye gṛhītvā tvaṃ prayaccha me
english: "'Through your line my line shall continue, O brāhmaṇa. Take this meal of mine and give it to the guest.'"

sanskrit: tava prasavanirvṛtyā mama lokāḥ kilākṣayāḥ pautreṇa tān avāpnoti yatra gatvā na śocati
english: "'By the continuance of your progeny, imperishable worlds will surely be mine; through a grandson one attains those worlds, going whither one grieves no more.'"

sanskrit: dharmādyā hi yathā tretā vahnitretā tathaiva ca tathaiva putrapautrāṇāṃ svarge tretā kilākṣayā
english: "'As the triad headed by righteousness, and likewise the triad of sacred fires, so too the triad of sons and grandsons is, in heaven, surely imperishable.'"

sanskrit: pitṝṃs trāṇāt tārayati putra ity anuśuśruma putrapautraiś ca niyataṃ sādhulokān upāśnute
english: "'A son delivers the ancestors because he saves them — so we have heard. And through sons and grandsons one assuredly enjoys the worlds of the righteous.'"

sanskrit: śvaśura uvāca vātātapaviśīrṇāṅgīṃ tvāṃ vivarṇāṃ nirīkṣya vai karśitāṃ suvratācāre kṣudhāvihvalacetasam
english: "The father-in-law said: 'Seeing you with your limbs wasted by wind and sun, pale and emaciated, O you of pious conduct, your mind distraught with hunger —'"

sanskrit: kathaṃ saktūn grahīṣyāmi bhūtvā dharmopaghātakaḥ kalyāṇavṛtte kalyāṇi naivaṃ tvaṃ vaktum arhasi
english: "'how shall I take your meal and so become a destroyer of righteousness? O auspicious one of blessed conduct, you ought not to speak thus.'"

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭhe kāle vratavatīṃ śīlaśaucasamanvitām kṛcchravṛttiṃ nirāhārāṃ drakṣyāmi tvāṃ kathaṃ nv aham
english: "'You who keep your vow until the sixth mealtime, endowed with good conduct and purity, living a hard life, without food — how could I bear to look upon you so?'"

sanskrit: bālā kṣudhārtā nārī ca rakṣyā tvaṃ satataṃ mayā upavāsapariśrāntā tvaṃ hi bāndhavanandinī
english: "'Young, hunger-stricken, and a woman, you are ever to be protected by me; for you, worn out by fasting, are the delight of our kin.'"

sanskrit: snuṣovāca guror mama gurus tvaṃ vai yato daivatadaivatam devātidevas tasmāt tvaṃ saktūn ādatsva me vibho
english: "The daughter-in-law said: 'You are the elder of my elder, the deity of deities, the god beyond gods; therefore take my meal, O lord.'"

sanskrit: dehaḥ prāṇaś ca dharmaś ca śuśrūṣārtham idaṃ guroḥ tava vipra prasādena lokān prāpsyāmy abhīpsitān
english: "'My body, my life-breath, and my merit — all this is for the service of my elder. By your grace, O brāhmaṇa, I shall attain the worlds I long for.'"

sanskrit: avekṣyā iti kṛtvā tvaṃ dṛḍhabhaktyeti vā dvija cintyā mameyam iti vā saktūn ādātum arhasi
english: "'Thinking either "she is to be regarded" or "she is of firm devotion," or else "she is one for whom I must provide," you ought, O brāhmaṇa, to take this meal.'"

sanskrit: śvaśura uvāca anena nityaṃ sādhvī tvaṃ śīlavṛttena śobhase yā tvaṃ dharmavratopetā guruvṛttim avekṣase
english: "The father-in-law said: 'By this ever-virtuous conduct of yours you shine, O good woman — you who, endowed with righteous vows, look to the service of your elders.'"

sanskrit: tasmāt saktūn grahīṣyāmi vadhūr nārhasi vañcanām gaṇayitvā mahābhāge tvaṃ hi dharmabhṛtāṃ varā
english: "'Therefore I will take your meal, O daughter-in-law; you do not deserve to be cheated of your due. Reckoned among them, O blessed one, you are the foremost of the upholders of righteousness.'"

sanskrit: ity uktvā tān upādāya saktūn prādād dvijātaye tatas tuṣṭo 'bhavad vipras tasya sādhor mahātmanaḥ
english: "So saying, he took up that meal and gave it to the brāhmaṇa; and then that brāhmaṇa was at last contented by the gift of that great-souled and righteous man."

sanskrit: prītātmā sa tu taṃ vākyam idam āha dvijarṣabham vāgmī tadā dvijaśreṣṭho dharmaḥ puruṣavigrahaḥ
english: "Glad of soul, that eloquent best of the twice-born — who was Dharma himself in human form — then spoke this word to the bull among brāhmaṇas:"

sanskrit: śuddhena tava dānena nyāyopāttena yatnataḥ yathāśakti vimuktena prīto 'smi dvijasattama
english: "'By your pure gift, righteously obtained with effort and given freely to the best of your power, I am well pleased, O excellent brāhmaṇa.'"

sanskrit: aho dānaṃ ghuṣyate te svarge svarganivāsibhiḥ gaganāt puṣpavarṣaṃ ca paśyasva patitaṃ bhuvi
english: "'Behold! Your gift is being proclaimed in heaven by the dwellers there; and see the rain of flowers falling from the sky upon the earth.'"

sanskrit: surarṣidevagandharvā ye ca devapuraḥsarāḥ stuvanto devadūtāś ca sthitā dānena vismitāḥ
english: "'The divine sages, gods, and gandharvas, and those who go before the gods, and the messengers of the gods, stand here singing your praises, amazed at your gift.'"

sanskrit: brahmarṣayo vimānasthā brahmalokagatāś ca ye kāṅkṣante darśanaṃ tubhyaṃ divaṃ gaccha dvijarṣabha
english: "'The brahmic sages seated in their celestial cars, and those who have gone to the world of Brahmā, long to behold you. Go to heaven, O bull among brāhmaṇas.'"

sanskrit: pitṛlokagatāḥ sarve tāritāḥ pitaras tvayā anāgatāś ca bahavaḥ subahūni yugāni ca
english: "'All your ancestors who have gone to the world of the fathers are delivered by you, and many more who are yet to come, through many ages hence.'"

sanskrit: brahmacaryeṇa yajñena dānena tapasā tathā agahvareṇa dharmeṇa tasmād gaccha divaṃ dvija
english: "'By chastity, by sacrifice, by giving, and likewise by austerity, and by guileless righteousness — therefore go to heaven, O brāhmaṇa.'"

sanskrit: śraddhayā parayā yas tvaṃ tapaś carasi suvrata tasmād devās tavānena prītā dvijavarottama
english: "'Because you, O man of firm vows, practise austerity with supreme faith, the gods are pleased with you for this, O most excellent of brāhmaṇas.'"

sanskrit: sarvasvam etad yasmāt te tyaktaṃ śuddhena cetasā kṛcchrakāle tataḥ svargo jito 'yaṃ tava karmaṇā
english: "'Since all this, your every possession, was given up with a pure heart in a time of dire need, by that deed of yours this heaven has been won.'"

sanskrit: kṣudhā nirṇudati prajñāṃ dharmyāṃ buddhiṃ vyapohati kṣudhāparigatajñāno dhṛtiṃ tyajati caiva ha
english: "'Hunger drives away wisdom and dispels the righteous mind; and one whose understanding is gripped by hunger forsakes even his firmness.'"

sanskrit: bubhukṣāṃ jayate yas tu sa svargaṃ jayate dhruvam yadā dānarucir bhavati tadā dharmo na sīdati
english: "'But whoever conquers the craving to eat surely conquers heaven; and when one delights in giving, then righteousness does not falter.'"

sanskrit: anavekṣya sutasnehaṃ kalatrasneham eva ca dharmam eva guruṃ jñātvā tṛṣṇā na gaṇitā tvayā
english: "'Disregarding love for your son and love for your wife, and knowing righteousness alone to be your true elder, you reckoned not your own craving.'"

sanskrit: dravyāgamo nṛṇāṃ sūkṣmaḥ pātre dānaṃ tataḥ param kālaḥ parataro dānāc chraddhā cāpi tataḥ parā
english: "'Slender is the acquiring of goods by men; greater than that is a gift to a worthy recipient; greater than the gift is the right time; and greater still than that is faith.'"

sanskrit: svargadvāraṃ susūkṣmaṃ hi narair mohān na dṛśyate svargārgalaṃ lobhabījaṃ rāgaguptaṃ durāsadam
english: "'The gate of heaven is exceeding subtle, and through delusion men do not see it. The bolt that bars heaven is the seed of greed, hidden by passion, hard to overcome.'"

sanskrit: tat tu paśyanti puruṣā jitakrodhā jitendriyāḥ brāhmaṇās tapasā yuktā yathāśaktipradāyinaḥ
english: "'But those men perceive that gate who have conquered anger and subdued their senses — brāhmaṇas yoked to austerity, who give according to their power.'"

sanskrit: sahasraśaktiś ca śataṃ śataśaktir daśāpi ca dadyād apaś ca yaḥ śaktyā sarve tulyaphalāḥ smṛtāḥ
english: "'He who can give a thousand and gives a hundred, he who can give a hundred and gives ten, and he who gives but water according to his power — all are held to reap an equal fruit.'"

sanskrit: rantidevo hi nṛpatir apaḥ prādād akiṃcanaḥ śuddhena manasā vipra nākapṛṣṭhaṃ tato gataḥ
english: "'For King Rantideva, having nothing, gave only water with a pure mind, O brāhmaṇa, and thereby went to the summit of heaven.'"

sanskrit: na dharmaḥ prīyate tāta dānair dattair mahāphalaiḥ nyāyalabdhair yathā sūkṣmaiḥ śraddhāpūtaiḥ sa tuṣyati
english: "'Righteousness is not so well pleased, my dear one, by gifts of great fruit that are given, as it is contented by slender gifts righteously obtained and hallowed by faith.'"

sanskrit: gopradānasahasrāṇi dvijebhyo 'dān nṛgo nṛpaḥ ekāṃ dattvā sa pārakyāṃ narakaṃ samavāptavān
english: "'King Nṛga gave thousands of cows to brāhmaṇas, yet by giving away a single cow that belonged to another he came to hell.'"

sanskrit: ātmamāṃsapradānena śibir auśīnaro nṛpaḥ prāpya puṇyakṛtāṃl lokān modate divi suvrataḥ
english: "'By the gift of his own flesh, King Śibi, the son of Uśīnara, attained the worlds of those who have done meritorious deeds, and that man of firm vows rejoices in heaven.'"
